title: Mycorrhizal Networks: Challenging the Simple 'Superhighway' Model of Nutrient Transfer
text:
The popular understanding depicts mycorrhizal networks primarily as a unidirectional superhighway, facilitating the mere transfer of limiting nutrients (like phosphate) from fungus to host root. Counter-intuitively, this view oversimplifies their complex role; these fungal systems are highly dynamic interfaces that do not merely shuttle resources but also mediate intense localized resource competition between connected plants.

Furthermore, the notion that connectivity guarantees universal mutual benefit is misleading. These underground filaments can transmit stress signals, defense elicitors, and even pathogens across spatially separated individuals, acting as a 'scaffolding' for biotic interactions rather than just benign plumbing. Therefore, assessing ecosystem health requires recognizing these networks not merely as conduits for sustenance, but as complex, multifaceted communication pathways with the potential for both crucial support and significant parasitic conflict.
